nodes.label: D-001: Implementations use DuckDB
nodes.rationale: Dataset is ~80 MB and fits in memory; DuckDB is columnar, close to BigQuery SQL, reads CSV/Parquet directly and needs no server. Rejected SQLite (row store), pandas-only (no SQL model) and BigQuery-first (cost and credentials before the model was known). Trade-off: BigQuery-only features cannot be shown.
nodes.status: Active, superseded in part by D-002 and D-003

nodes.label: D-003: Idiomatic DuckDB SQL
nodes.rationale: D-001 asked for BigQuery-portable SQL, which rules out convenient DuckDB functions and hurts readability. With no cloud phase (D-002) portability has no user; translation work is listed in DATA_MODEL.md if ever needed. Trade-off: a BigQuery move needs dialect translation, not copy-paste.

nodes.label: D-005: No Prometheus, Grafana or FastAPI
nodes.norm_label: d-005: no prometheus, grafana or fastapi
nodes.rationale: There is no long-running service to monitor or serve; the build is a batch job that passes its checks or exits non-zero. Trade-off: no live dashboards or prediction endpoint; model outputs are files and notebook results.

nodes.label: DD-01: Kimball star schema; facts never join to facts
nodes.norm_label: dd-01: kimball star schema; facts never join to facts
nodes.rationale: Joining items, payments and reviews side by side overstated item revenue by 4.54% (5.02% with reviews) in the EDA. One stated grain per fact; facts meet only through dimensions or after aggregation. Rejected a wide table (silent fan-out).

nodes.label: DD-02: Customer grain is `customer_unique_id`
nodes.rationale: customer_id is issued per order: 99,441 ids belong to 96,096 people. Using it would make every customer look like a one-time buyer. Location at order time is carried on facts because 250 customers moved.

nodes.label: DD-06: Convert geolocation CSV to Parquet in the build
nodes.norm_label: dd-06: convert geolocation csv to parquet in the build
nodes.rationale: Kaggle ships geolocation as a ~1M row CSV but staging reads Parquet; ensure_geolocation_parquet converts once and keeps zip prefixes as text so leading zeros survive. Not yet tested against Kaggle's original download.

nodes.label: DD-07: Customer segmentation is optional
nodes.rationale: 96.9% of customers ordered once so frequency-based clusters carry little information. K-Means is tried honestly and dropped if it adds little; RFM segmentation rejected as an up-front commitment.

nodes.label: DD-11: No recalibration or window tuning; use the model by rank
nodes.norm_label: dd-11: no recalibration or window tuning; use the model by rank
nodes.rationale: Recalibration worsened Brier, log loss and calibration error in every variant (recent late rate vs next month correlation -0.18); walk-forward window gain +0.010 PR-AUC won in only 3 of 6 months, mostly August 2018. A change is adopted only if it beats the reference out-of-time. Operating point is a share of orders flagged, not a probability cut-off.

nodes.label: D-002: Local only, no GCP
nodes.rationale: A cloud phase needs a GCP project, billing, IAM and gcloud that add cost, credential risk and setup time without adding evidence for the data model and ML work. DuckDB stands in for BigQuery. Trade-off: no cloud deployment to show; Dataflow/Beam and BigQuery region questions become moot; cloud pricing stays unverified.

nodes.label: D-004: No dbt, plain SQL run by a Python script
nodes.norm_label: d-004: no dbt, plain sql run by a python script
nodes.rationale: Fewer moving parts; the build order is small and explicit. Trade-off: no dbt lineage graph, docs site or built-in tests, but table constraints and sql/validation/checks.sql cover the same ground.

nodes.label: D-006: .gitignore covers database, data/ and credentials
nodes.norm_label: d-006: .gitignore covers database, data/ and credentials
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 found no .gitignore and data/ tracked. The database is rebuilt from source, raw data is re-downloadable, and credentials must never be committed.

nodes.label: D-007: ML target is late delivery plus weekly order forecast
nodes.norm_label: d-007: ml target is late delivery plus weekly order forecast
nodes.rationale: Late-delivery label comes straight from timestamps with no review dependency; features at purchase are concrete (seller, product size, freight, route, promised window); late orders average 2.57 stars vs 4.29 on time. Rejected low review score (highest leakage risk) and repeat purchase (~3.1% positives, censored window). Trade-off: 8.1% positive class so accuracy is meaningless; PR metrics needed.

nodes.label: D-008: Untrack data/ from Git, do not rewrite history
nodes.norm_label: d-008: untrack data/ from git, do not rewrite history
nodes.rationale: Nine raw files were tracked before D-006; pushing them redistributes a CC BY-NC-SA dataset. Untracking stops future commits carrying data without a destructive force-push history rewrite. Trade-off: earlier commits still contain the files (commit d8f6954).

nodes.label: DD-08: Add scikit-learn for ML baselines
nodes.norm_label: dd-08: add scikit-learn for ml baselines
nodes.rationale: Standard, well-tested implementations of logistic regression and gradient boosting; a baseline that has to be debugged is a poor baseline. Rejected hand-written models and rate-only baselines (cannot show what a feature-based model adds). scikit-learn 1.9.1.

nodes.label: DD-09: Report backtest metrics as per-month macro-average
nodes.norm_label: dd-09: report backtest metrics as per-month macro-average
nodes.rationale: A first pooled backtest gave the constant baseline a ROC-AUC of 0.36 because pooling ranks different months' constants against each other. Each month is scored by a model trained at one date and the late rate swings 1.4% to 21.4%. Trade-off: low-volume months count as much as large ones.

nodes.label: DD-10: Keep v1 features as the reference late-delivery model
nodes.norm_label: dd-10: keep v1 features as the reference late-delivery model
nodes.rationale: v2 (route/category history) and v3 (trailing 28-day rate) lowered logistic PR-AUC from 0.184 to 0.174 and 0.178 and worsened top-end calibration; a model should not get more complex without a measured gain. v2/v3 stay in the SQL so the comparison can be rerun. Drift analysis later showed v3 and category fail on regime, route history fails on redundancy with v1.

nodes.label: DD-12: Close ML experiments; v1 and simple forecasts are final
nodes.norm_label: dd-12: close ml experiments; v1 and simple forecasts are final
nodes.rationale: Slack features did not beat v1 (PR-AUC 0.176 vs 0.184) and no forecast model clearly beat simple averages on an 85-week backtest. Four feature ideas and two post-hoc fixes were tried on the same six test months; continuing would mostly fit noise, and remaining phases (analytics, docs, audit) matter more. Forecast recommendation: average of naive and 8-week average at 1 week, 8-week average at 4 weeks.

nodes.label: warehouse.duckdb (single local database file)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt from scratch every run (~25 s) so there is no migration logic or state to drift.

nodes.label: Late delivery vs review score association (4.29 on time, 2.57 late)
nodes.norm_label: late delivery vs review score association (4.29 on time, 2.57 late)
nodes.rationale: Orders more than 3 days late are 5.2% of reviewed deliveries but only ~30% of 1-2 star reviews; ~70% come from on-time orders. An earlier draft claimed the opposite and was corrected in the audit.

nodes.label: 2018 delivery promise shortened (75% of August orders under 20 days)
nodes.norm_label: 2018 delivery promise shortened (75% of august orders under 20 days)
nodes.rationale: Late rate rose to 10.5% in August even as median delivery fell to 7.0 days, because the promise shortened more; late rate peaked at 21% in March 2018 and dropped to 1.4% in June.

nodes.label: August 2018 delivery-promise policy shift
nodes.rationale: 72% of non-canceled August orders were promised in under 20 days with a 13.9% late rate; concept drift in a plain v1 feature (promised days, within-month ROC-AUC 0.186) that made August the weakest month for every model. Cause of the policy change is not in the data.

nodes.label: E2: persistence of route/category/seller lateness
nodes.rationale: Routes are stable P2 to P3 (Spearman 0.70, near noise ceiling 0.85); categories are not; sellers persist only P2 to P3.

nodes.label: E5: oracle true month late rate ceiling
nodes.norm_label: e5: oracle true month late rate ceiling
nodes.rationale: Giving the model the true month rate leaves PR-AUC unchanged (0.1837 to 0.1839) while Brier drops 9% (0.0778 to 0.0711): system drift is a calibration problem, not a ranking problem.

nodes.label: E6: route history redundant with state and distance
nodes.norm_label: e6: route history redundant with state and distance
nodes.rationale: Without geography route history recovers half of the lost 0.067 PR-AUC, but on top of full v1 it lowers PR-AUC by ~0.009: informative and stable yet already present in v1.

nodes.label: v4: relative route/category rate features
nodes.rationale: Beat v2 in all four windows by 0.002 to 0.011 but never beat v1.

nodes.label: Forecast recommendation: naive+8-week average (1wk), 8-week average (4wk)
nodes.rationale: Combination was assembled after seeing baseline results so its edge is optimistic; beat naive in only 51% of weeks. AR(1) ranks among best on revenue and worst on orders, showing the 85-week backtest cannot separate models.

nodes.label: Late-delivery model v1 (logistic regression)
nodes.rationale: Logistic regression on 16 numeric and 3 categorical purchase-time features; PR-AUC 0.184, ROC-AUC 0.707, Brier 0.0778, precision 0.207 and recall 0.279 at top 10% flagged. Intended for triage by rank, not for quoting probabilities.

nodes.label: Use model by rank: flag riskiest 10% (lift 2.8x)
nodes.norm_label: use model by rank: flag riskiest 10% (lift 2.8x)
nodes.rationale: Probabilities are off in level by ~0.06 per month (0.14 in March 2018) because the late rate swings 1.4% to 21.4%; a fixed cut-off would flag too many orders in high-rate months. Lift averages 2.8x and was 1.2x in August 2018.

nodes.label: v5: delivery-time slack features
nodes.rationale: Promised days minus how long the route and the system have recently taken; no gain (PR-AUC 0.176 vs 0.184), top-quintile calibration somewhat closer (0.191 predicted vs 0.165 actual).

nodes.label: Forecast baselines: naive, moving averages, linear trend
nodes.norm_label: forecast baselines: naive, moving averages, linear trend

nodes.label: Gradient boosting baseline (depth 4)
nodes.rationale: Did not beat the linear model (PR-AUC 0.172 vs 0.184), so improvement is more likely from better features than a bigger model.

nodes.label: Seller history rate baseline
nodes.rationale: ROC-AUC 0.526, near coin flip: late deliveries cluster in time more than they stick to sellers.

nodes.label: v2: route and category late-rate history features
nodes.norm_label: v2: route and category late-rate history features
nodes.rationale: Logistic PR-AUC fell to 0.174; extra history made the model more confident without making it more right. Later shown redundant with v1 state and distance columns.

nodes.label: v3: trailing 28-day system late rate feature
nodes.norm_label: v3: trailing 28-day system late rate feature
nodes.rationale: Logistic PR-AUC 0.178, Brier 0.0859; drift analysis showed it tracks regime, with within-month ROC-AUC 0.446 on test.

nodes.label: Recalibration experiment (level shift, Platt, isotonic)
nodes.rationale: No variant beat the reference on Brier, log loss or calibration error: recent late rate does not predict next month's, and holding orders out for calibration makes the base model staler (PR-AUC 0.184 to 0.176/0.166).

nodes.label: Training-window tuning experiment
nodes.rationale: 2-month window looked best (0.205) only in hindsight; walk-forward choice gained +0.010 PR-AUC, won 3 of 6 months, +0.070 in August 2018 alone; chosen window jumped 3,4,6,6,2,2.

nodes.label: Phase 0 cloud architecture proposal (GCS, BigQuery, Dataflow, Vertex AI)
nodes.norm_label: phase 0 cloud architecture proposal (gcs, bigquery, dataflow, vertex ai)
nodes.rationale: Minimal viable cloud architecture proposed with Dataflow assessed as unnecessary for ~80 MB; later made moot by D-002.

nodes.label: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce dataset (Kaggle, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
nodes.norm_label: olist brazilian e-commerce dataset (kaggle, cc by-nc-sa 4.0)
nodes.rationale: Nine files, ~100k orders from 2016-09-04 to 2018-10-17, ~80 MB; the whole dataset fits in laptop memory, the key architecture fact.

nodes.label: Unverified BigQuery, Dataflow and Vertex AI pricing
nodes.norm_label: unverified bigquery, dataflow and vertex ai pricing

nodes.label: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence constraints

nodes.label: DD-03: Reviews keyed on (review_id, order_id) with latest-review flag
nodes.norm_label: dd-03: reviews keyed on (review_id, order_id) with latest-review flag
nodes.rationale: review_id is not unique (789 ids span several orders) and 547 orders have 2-3 reviews. Deleting duplicates would lose source rows, so an is_latest_review_for_order flag is used instead.

nodes.label: DD-04: Revenue measured from order items only
nodes.norm_label: dd-04: revenue measured from order items only
nodes.rationale: Payments differ from items plus freight on 380 of 98,665 orders, mostly instalment orders, so fact_payments is analysed on its own and never forced to tie. Rejected payment value as revenue and reconciling by adjustment.

nodes.label: DD-05: Surrogate keys with an unknown member (-1)
nodes.norm_label: dd-05: surrogate keys with an unknown member (-1)
nodes.rationale: 279 customer rows have a zip prefix missing from geolocation and some milestone dates are null; a -1 unknown member in every dimension means a failed lookup never drops a fact row. Rejected inner joins that drop rows and null foreign keys.

nodes.label: dim_geography (one row per zip prefix, 19,012 rows)
nodes.norm_label: dim_geography (one row per zip prefix, 19,012 rows)

nodes.label: review_id is not unique (789 ids on several orders)
nodes.norm_label: review_id is not unique (789 ids on several orders)

nodes.label: Purchase-time prediction point and column audit
nodes.norm_label: purchase-time prediction point and column audit
nodes.rationale: Columns classified allowed, point-in-time, post-outcome, target-derived, identifier or high-cardinality; shipping_limit_date is set at approval so excluded; all review fields are post-outcome.

nodes.label: Time-ordered split with gap
nodes.rationale: A random split would mix regimes (monthly late rate 1.4% to 21.4%) and hide drift; a gap of 2-3 weeks keeps training labels from resolving inside the test period.
